body:
This pull request was created by @kiro-agent on behalf of @SayanMazumder75 :ghost:

Comment with **/kiro fix** to address specific feedback or **/kiro all** to address everything.
<sub>[Learn about Kiro Web](https://kiro.dev/web/)</sub>

---
## Summary

Port the auth pattern from the [speech-to-text repo](https://github.com/SayanMazumder75/speechtotext) verbatim and apply it to LIVE. AI Transcriber doesn't host its own login page — when embedded inside MeetMind, the parent page broadcasts a JWT to the iframe via `postMessage`, exactly like the speech-to-text repo. The token rides on every backend request as `Authorization: Bearer`, and **the History UI is gated on token presence**. Live transcription itself is unaffected.

A single MeetMind broadcast authenticates both apps simultaneously because the wire format (`{ type: "MEETMIND_AUTH", token }`) is identical.

## Changes

### New files

- **`frontend/src/auth.js`** — SSO token bridge. Listens for `MEETMIND_AUTH` postMessage from `VITE_MEETMIND_ORIGIN` (strict origin check), caches the token in memory + `localStorage["live_auth_token"]`, exports `getToken()` / `clearToken()` / `subscribe()` / `isAuthenticated()`. Separate localStorage key from speechtotext's `stt_auth_token` so a 401 in one app doesn't sign the user out of the other; both apps still receive the same broadcast in real time.
- **`frontend/src/hooks/useAuth.js`** — thin React hook returning `{ token, isAuthenticated }` that subscribes to the auth store so UI gating re-renders on token arrival/clear.

### Modified files

- **`frontend/src/main.jsx`** — `import "./auth.js";` is now the very first line, mirroring speech-to-text's `main.jsx`. The postMessage listener has to be registered before React mounts.
- **`frontend/src/hooks/useSessionPersistence.js`** — every fetch goes through a new `authHeaders()` helper that attaches `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>` when the bridge has a token. Covers all five sites: `_get`, `_post` (start-session, push, transcripts, transcript/:id, insights), the `GET /` probe, `POST /upload-audio` (multipart — doesn't override `Content-Type`), and `DELETE /transcript/:id`. On `401` the hook calls `clearToken()` so MeetMind can re-broadcast a fresh token without us caching the stale one.
- **`frontend/src/App.jsx`** — imports `useAuth`, gates UI:
  - **Header History button** — disabled with tooltip *"Sign in via MeetMind to view session history"* when not authenticated. The session-active dot is hidden when signed out.
  - **Saved-banner "Open another" button** — hidden when not authenticated.
  - **Auto-close** — if the token is cleared while the drawer is open (e.g. backend 401 mid-session), `setHistoryOpen(false)` runs so the user isn't staring at a list they can't refresh.
  - Live transcription, Start/Stop, mic toggle, Save Insights, etc. are all untouched.
- **`frontend/.env.example`** *(new)* — documents `VITE_MEETMIND_ORIGIN`, `VITE_HTTP_URL`, `VITE_WS_URL`, and tuning knobs.
- **`README.md`** — new *Authentication — SSO bridge from MeetMind* section explaining the contract, the MeetMind-side broadcast snippet, the strict-origin guarantee, the localStorage key, the 401 behaviour, and the configuration.

## Wire protocol (matches speech-to-text)

MeetMind → iframe:

```js
iframe.contentWindow.postMessage(
  { type: "MEETMIND_AUTH", token: "<jwt>" },
  "https://ai-transcriber.example.com" // exact iframe origin
);
```

Iframe → backend (every request):

```
Authorization: Bearer <jwt>
```

## Configuration

Set per-environment in `frontend/.env.local`:

```
# Production
VITE_MEETMIND_ORIGIN=https://meetmind.vercel.app

# Local dev (MeetMind on Next.js default)
VITE_MEETMIND_ORIGIN=http://localhost:3000
```

The bridge falls back to `https://meetmind.vercel.app` when unset. Use `VITE_MEETMIND_ORIGIN=*` only for local-network testing — the README calls this out explicitly.

## Tested

- `npm run build` succeeds (vite v5.4.21, 1789 modules, no warnings).
- All five fetch sites in `useSessionPersistence.js` confirmed via grep to use `authHeaders()` and handle 401.
- Branch is rebased on the current `main` (post-PR-#30 merge that removed `FloatingMicWidget`); App.jsx changes apply cleanly to the new file.

## Not tested in this environment

- Live MeetMind handshake (no parent page in the build sandbox to send a real `MEETMIND_AUTH`). Worth a manual smoke test: load AI Transcriber inside MeetMind, broadcast a JWT → History button should enable, requests should carry the Bearer header. Force a 401 from the backend → button should re-disable and the drawer should close.
- Backend-side JWT verification is intentionally out of scope — this PR only sends the header. The LIVE backend currently accepts requests without auth, so existing standalone deployments keep working (History stays hidden until a token arrives, but live transcription is unaffected).

## Problem
Under `tsx` (every CLI script), `(await import("@/lib/verification/renderUrl")).renderUrl` is `undefined` — the dynamic import returns a CJS-interop namespace `{ default, "module.exports" }` with the named exports under `.default`. The extractor's `try/catch` can't catch it (the import *succeeds*), so `render` silently became `undefined` and **every script-run extraction (`seed:enrich`, `reextract:stubs`, `audit:bare-windows`, `adjudicate:flags`) ran plain-fetch-only**. JS-SPA homepages and robots-walled menu links were never rendered → their happy hours dropped. The five `closeRenderBrowser()` teardown sites hit the same trap and threw `is not a function` at exit, leaking Chromium.

Next.js runtime (webpack interop) was unaffected — this is tsx-scripts-only, but scripts do all the bulk extraction.

## Fix
`lib/verification/lazyRender.ts` — a statically-imported wrapper that normalises the interop (`mod.renderUrl ?? mod.default.renderUrl`) and still defers Playwright via its own internal dynamic import (Next bundle stays clean). All 7 call sites updated. `test:lazy-render` guards the regression.

author: llmpsycho
body:
## Summary

Memory scopes keyed on the current directory name, so a single project fragmented across git worktrees, clones, forks, and renamed directories — and unrelated directories that happened to share a basename collided into the same memory. This introduces a stable project identity used everywhere memory is scoped.

When `memory.projectKey` is unset, OMP auto-detects identity from git. Set it (or `OMP_PROJECT_KEY` / `HINDSIGHT_PROJECT_KEY`) to force one shared identity such as `github.com/org/repo` across machines and checkouts.

### Resolver order

1. Explicit key: `OMP_PROJECT_KEY`, `HINDSIGHT_PROJECT_KEY`, then the `memory.projectKey` setting.
2. Git remote URL — prefers `upstream`, then `origin`, then the first valid remote. HTTPS, SSH/SCP, and plain `host/org/repo` forms normalize to lowercase `host/org/repo` with a trailing `.git` stripped.
3. Shared git common-dir identity, so linked worktrees and bare-repo checkouts of one repo share a key.
4. Path-hashed cwd fallback (basename + hash) outside any repository.

### Where it applies

- Hindsight `per-project` bank ids and `per-project-tagged` `project:<key>` tags.
- Local memory roots and `memory://root` resolution.
- Mnemopi per-project banks.

### Notable decisions

- Filesystem-safe segments append a short hash suffix, so two distinct keys (e.g. `org/repo-a` vs `org-repo/a`) can never collapse to the same directory or bank name.
- `file://` and local filesystem remotes are not treated as hosted identities; only URL/SCP-like remotes produce a remote key. Plain `host/org/repo` is still valid as an explicit setting value.
- Local git identity canonicalizes the common dir (`/var` vs `/private/var`) so it hashes consistently across symlinked temp roots.

### Backward compatibility

Installs with the setting unset keep working via auto-detection. On startup the local-memory pipeline migrates the active project's thread rows to the resolved key and re-enqueues phase2 consolidation, so processed outputs are not stranded under the old cwd key. Scoped clear removes both the new project-key rows/roots and the legacy cwd-scoped ones.

### Tests

`bun test` across memory project identity, Hindsight bank scoping, memory tools, storage migration/clear, memories isolation/runtime, and the `memory://` protocol — 94 pass, 0 fail. `bun --cwd=packages/coding-agent run check` and `run build` are green.

body:
## What

Closes #213. PULL fetched only the original issue body (`gh issue list`), so the triager + implementer were blind to human follow-up posted as **comments** — where the most current guidance often lives.

## Changes
- **WorkItem** gains an additive `comments` field (`[{author, created_at, body}]`); `WORK_ITEM_SCHEMA_VERSION` -> `1.1.0`.
- Carried through TRIAGE onto the **WorkOrder** (the implementer reads `work_orders`, not `work_items`); `WORK_ORDER_SCHEMA_VERSION` -> `1.1.0`.
- Comments are **fetched per pulled issue** via `gh issue view <n> --json comments` (gh `issue list` does not return them). The subprocess `runner` is injectable (determinism seam, mirroring `gh_issue_source`/`gh_issue_file_sink`); a per-issue fetch failure is **tolerated** (empty `comments`) so a flaky read never sinks PULL.
- **Bounded**: most-recent `MAX_COMMENTS_PER_ITEM` (=20), each body capped at `MAX_COMMENT_BODY_CHARS` (=4000), so a long thread cannot bloat the rendered envelope.
- The field **renders automatically** into the triager/implementer envelopes (agent-dispatch `render` is generic over the slot dict); the shipped `auto-maintainer-triager` prompt now tells the judge to read comments, not just the body.

author: restitutio777
body:
## Worum geht's

Die Site hat viele Räume (schreibBAR, denkBAR, bewegBAR, machBAR, lesBAR, brauchBAR, hörBAR, wunderBAR). Bisher musste ein Besucher jeden Raum einzeln öffnen, um zu sehen, wo es etwas Neues gibt. Dieser PR ergänzt die Landing-Page um eine schlichte Liste **„Zuletzt veröffentlicht"**, die quer durch alle Räume die jüngsten Beiträge zeigt — jeder mit Direktlink.

## Wie es funktioniert

- **Eine GROQ-Query** holt zur Build-Zeit die drei jüngsten Einträge über alle sechs Dokument-Typen (`note`, `station`, `event`, `resource`, `episode`, `wonder`), sortiert nach `_updatedAt` — Sanitys Zeitpunkt der letzten Veröffentlichung. So taucht jeder neue Publish automatisch oben auf. `defined(slug.current)` stellt sicher, dass nur verlinkbare Einträge erscheinen.
- **`roomFor()`** spiegelt die bestehende Routing-Logik der Detail-Seiten: `note`/`event`/`resource` verzweigen je nach `kind` nach schreibBAR/denkBAR, machBAR/denkBAR bzw. lesBAR/brauchBAR. Liefert Label, Akzentfarbe und URL-Basis.
- **Datum:** wird client-seitig zu einer relativen Angabe („vor 3 Tagen") — wichtig, weil die Site statisch ist und ein fest gerendertes „heute" sonst am Deploy-Tag einfrieren würde. Ohne JS bleibt das absolute Datum als Fallback stehen.

Kein neuer Sanity-Schema-Bedarf, keine DB-Migration — nur eine zusätzliche Lese-Query über den bereits konfigurierten öffentlichen Client.

## Design

Bewusst **kein** Kachel-Grid (sonst Doppelung mit der Raum-Übersicht „Wohin als nächstes?" darunter): nur drei ruhige Textzeilen — Titel + Raum · Datum, jede ein Direktlink, getrennt durch feine Hairlines. Beim Hover färbt sich der Titel in die Raum-Akzentfarbe. Liest sich als „was ist neu", nicht als zweite Navigation.

## Test

`npm run build` läuft durch (33 Seiten). Die Liste rendert mit echten Sanity-Daten korrekt — verifiziert in `dist/index.html`: 3 Einträge, korrekte Detail-Links, absteigend nach Veröffentlichungsdatum.

- 기존 배포는 Pod가 `Running` 상태가 되면 성공처럼 보였지만, 실제 사용자 요청 기준의 오류율과 지연 회귀를 막는 장치가 없었습니다.

author: nao1215
body:
## Summary

v1.3.0 added a per-package `--timeout` that defaults to 5 minutes, which kills a perfectly healthy `go install` whose compile simply takes longer than that (large dependency trees, slow machines, a cold module cache), so `gup update` reports `install timed out: context deadline exceeded` where v1.2.0 always succeeded. This restores the v1.2.0 behavior by making the default no timeout (`0`), keeping `--timeout` as an opt-in bound, and makes the timeout error name the exact command to run and how to relax the limit. ref #318

## Changes

- `cmd/precheck.go`: change `defaultGoOpTimeout` to `time.Duration(0)` (no timeout by default) and update its doc comment; the explicit type keeps the `time` import in use.
- `cmd/flags.go`: update the `--timeout` help text to say the default `0` means no timeout.
- `internal/goutil/goutil.go`: on timeout, `InstallWithContext` now includes `go install <path>@<version>` and `GetVerWithContext` includes `go list -m <module>@<ref>`, both with a `--timeout` hint, while still wrapping the context error with `%w`.
- `cmd/flags_test.go`: assert the default timeout is `0` explicitly so re-introducing a non-zero default is caught.
- `internal/goutil/goutil_test.go`: assert the timeout errors carry the runnable command, the `--timeout` hint, and `context.DeadlineExceeded`.

## Design Decisions

A default timeout on `go install` is fundamentally fragile because compile time is unbounded and machine-dependent, so any fixed default eventually kills legitimate builds; disabling it by default matches v1.2.0 exactly and is a behavior restoration rather than a new risk. Signal-based cancellation (Ctrl-C) is independent of `--timeout`, so an actually stuck subprocess can still be aborted, and users who want a hard bound (CI, flaky proxies) keep it via `--timeout 5m`. The error improvement lives in `internal/goutil` because that is where the user-facing message is already built and where both the import path/version and module/ref are in scope; only the timeout branch is touched (cancel is user-initiated, and the empty-stderr case was handled separately). The cancel branch and the generic failure message are intentionally left unchanged. CHANGELOG.md is not touched here because this repository updates it during release preparation, and the `fix(cmd):` commit prefix feeds the generated GitHub release notes.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Documentation**
  * Updated the `--timeout` flag help text to clarify that a default value of `0` disables the timeout completely.

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Improved timeout error messages to include concrete manual command suggestions and guidance on the `--timeout` flag for resolving timeout issues.

* **Chores**
  * Changed the default timeout from 5 minutes to disabled (0).

author: esterkane
body:
## What

Adds an **MCP server** exposing the planner/explain core as agent tools, built on the official TypeScript MCP SDK (`@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`). Tools: `plan(query)` and `explain(query)` (read-only) and `reload_policies()` (mutating, gated).

## Design

- **Thin adapters only.** Tool *logic* lives in `src/mcp/tools.ts` as pure async functions taking explicit deps (`createPlan`, `explainPlan`, `loadPolicies`, the live policy set) — unit-testable without a live Elasticsearch. `src/mcp/server.ts` is a thin SDK adapter (stdio transport); `src/mcp/errors.ts` is the structured result/error contract.
- **Same shapes as the routes.** Tools return the exact objects `POST /plan`, `POST /explain`, and `POST /policies/reload` return — `source_policy_id` on every clause plus `policy_trace` / `conflict_trace` provenance preserved. Inputs are Zod-validated with the repo's existing `planRequestSchema`.

author: avrabe
body:
## What

Frozen-safe north-star increment (epic #242, VCR-PERF-001 / VCR-RA-010). Reproduces gale #390's **headline Pass-1** waste — "every wasm local/operand spilled to a stack slot, `sched` reloaded 10×, ~288 B / 47%" — on synth's **own frozen fixtures**, so the spill waste is regression-tracked in-tree (not only on gale's gust silicon), and the eventual spill-eliminating wiring has a measurable target.

**Zero codegen change.** Adds:
- `scripts/repro/spill_baseline_measure.sh` — compiles the three frozen fixtures and reads the emitted ARM (thumb objdump) + the existing `SYNTH_SHADOW_ALLOC` instrumentation.
- A roadmap note under VCR-PERF-001 recording the baseline + the finding.

## Measured (debug binary, 2026-06-21)

| fixture | insns | spill `[sp,#]` | linmem `[fp/r11]` | peak value-pressure |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| flight_seam_flat | 356 | **56** | 42 | **7** (≤9) |
| flight_seam | 300 | **39** | 28 | 7–8 |
| control_step | 113 | **6** | 2 | 8 |

## Finding

The `[sp,#]` spills are **spurious**: synth keeps WASM locals frame-resident *by model* (`local.get`→`ldr [sp]`, `local.set`→`str [sp]`), **not** from register pressure — peak *value*-pressure ≤ 9 means every live value fits the R0–R8 pool. The value-based allocator (VCR-RA-001, today shadow-only behind `SYNTH_SHADOW_ALLOC`) eliminates them. The default-on range-realloc (`reallocate_function`, v0.11.36) is a *renamer* — it never adds/removes instructions, so it provably cannot capture Pass-1; `apply_const_cse` is flag-gated. So Pass-1 is genuinely unrealized in default codegen — #390's headline holds.

**Resolves the const-CSE-vs-spill fork with data:** const/remat opportunities are 0–2 on these kernels (synth already lowers consts as immediates), while spill-elimination is 56/39/6. The spill axis is where the bytes are, and it's independent of the const-remat axis.

## Frozen-safe

Script + roadmap note only; frozen fixtures (control_step `0x00210A55`, flat+inlined flight_algo `0x07FDF307`, divseam) byte-identical by construction. The byte-changing wiring remains a **separate gated step** — deliberate re-freeze + differential + gale on-silicon (the #193/#212/#215 latent-regalloc lesson).

## What

Routes every value cell of `DataManager.exportToCSV()` through the shared SSOT encoder `window.CsvSafe.cell` (`apps/admin-panel/js/core/csv-safe.js`, introduced by #384) instead of the raw `"${cell}"` wrap that had **NO quote-doubling and NO formula guard** — the **LAST live admin-panel CSV sink** (same class as the merged #386 ClientsTable). A user `username`/`name`/`email`/`role` beginning with `= + - @` executed as a formula when the admin opened the download; a stray `"` broke the CSV.

Adds a fail-secure `ensureCsvSafe()` guard: if the encoder is not loaded, the export aborts with a Hebrew notice rather than emit un-neutralized CSV. Faithful mirror of merged precedent #386 — **route, never copy (encoders are SSOT)**.

This closes the CSV-injection sub-track (#384 SMS, #385 ReportGenerator, #386 ClientsTable, this = DataManager).

## Scope / Reachability (security-access-expert lens)

- `exportToCSV` is wired LIVE from the "ייצוא" button in `FilterBar.js` (`attachExportButton` -> `window.DataManager.exportToCSV()`), and FilterBar is loaded **only on `index.html`** — where `csv-safe.js` is already present (line 238).
- The other two pages loading `DataManager.js` (`workload.html`, `employee-costs.html`) do **not** load FilterBar -> the export button is unreachable there, so **no `<script>` change is needed**; `ensureCsvSafe` is the fail-secure backstop regardless.
- Hardcoded Hebrew headers (`headers.join(',')`) have no formula trigger -> left as-is.
- Diff limited to `exportToCSV` + the new `ensureCsvSafe` method + the test + the rubric (+30/-1 in DataManager.js).

## Test plan (G4)

`tests/unit/admin-panel/datamanager-csv-injection.test.ts` (vitest + happy-dom, Blob-capture integration):
- poisoned `=HYPERLINK("..")` / `+` / `-` / `@` name/email/role cells -> inert (formula-prefixed + RFC-4180 quote-doubled), no quoted cell opens onto a live trigger;
- benign Hebrew (`משה לוי`) unchanged — no false-positive `'`;
- fail-secure: encoder missing -> export aborts (`captured===''`) + Hebrew notice.

6/6 new pass; full admin-panel suite **143/143** (137 prior + 6).

## Reviews

- **outcomes-grader = PASS** (6/6 MUST, 2/2 SHOULD, 7/7 gates; independent read of the files; confirmed faithful mirror of #386, scope-disciplined, fail-secure, G4-proven).
- security-access-expert lens (OWASP CSV/formula injection): SSOT-routed, fail-secure.
- Rubric: `.claude/rubrics/pr-datamanager-csv-injection.md`.

## Rollback

`git revert <merge-commit>` + redeploy (frontend; Netlify auto-redeploys from main). No data migration, no schema/rule/claim change. Reverting restores the prior `exportToCSV` cell line + removes `ensureCsvSafe`; `csv-safe.js` (#384) untouched. Executable in under 5 minutes.

- **G4 PASS** — Blob-capture integration test proves poisoned cells inert + fail-secure abort.
- **G5 PASS** — Hebrew customer-facing error notice; `console.*` lines are dev-only (acceptable).
- **G6 N/A** — no contract/schema/route change; CSV byte-identical for benign data (only malicious/quote-containing values newly neutralized — a fix, not a break).

author: com-junkawasaki
body:
## Summary

Broadens the Clojure-language surface of `kotoba-clj` (the Clojure/EDN-subset → WASM AOT compiler) with **no new codegen path** beyond one branch peephole — everything else is pure-subset `PRELUDE` functions (compiled through the existing vec/map + closure-table machinery) or AST desugars into existing special forms.

Two commits:

### 1. clojure.core stdlib + iteration sugars (`e59f60ba`)
- **New special forms** (`ast.rs` desugar): `while`, `dotimes`, `doseq` (single binding) → `loop`/`recur`; `if-some`/`when-some` aliased to the let-binding forms (nil≡0≡falsy in the i64 model).
- **New PRELUDE fns**: `take` `drop` `take-while` `drop-while` `butlast` `take-last` `reverse` `concat` `repeat` `interpose` `interleave` `partition` `vec-contains?` `distinct` `sort` `sort-by` `merge` `merge-with` `select-keys` `zipmap` `get-in` `update` `complement` `juxt` `fnil` `max-key` `min-key`; `vector` arity extended 4→8.

### 2. Strings, 2-pass collections, branch peephole (`5ed286e9`)
- **Strings** (PRELUDE, on the byte-builder): `str-cat`, `subs` (2/3-arity), `str-starts-with?`, `str-includes?`, `str-join` (single-alloc), `str-int` (signed int → decimal). No generic variadic `str` (the i64 model has no runtime type tags to distinguish an int handle from a string handle).
- **2-pass / pre-sized collections**: `mapcat` (sum-then-concat), `frequencies`, `group-by` (string-keyed maps).
- **Branch peephole** (`codegen.rs`): `compile_truthy_i32` feeds a 2-arg comparison (`= != < > <= >=`) straight into `if`/`br_if`, dropping the `extend_i32_u; const 0; i64.ne` round-trip the i64-everything model emitted. `fib` body **20 → 17 instrs, 34 → 30 B**.

## Honest limits (the i64 / mutable-bump model, unchanged)
- `distinct`/`vec-contains?` compare scalars by value, collection/string handles by identity.
- Map fns assume **string keys** (the `str-eq?` contract).
- `sort` is O(n²) selection sort; no number tower (i64 only); no lazy seqs / persistent structures; no dead-code elimination (a prelude-on module grew ~5.5 KB → ~8.7 KB — negligible for agents, a DCE target later).
- **Peephole perf (measured):** shrinks module size + instruction count but does **not** change `fib` steady-state on optimizing JITs — wasmtime/Cranelift and V8/TurboFan already fold the round-trip (fib(32) stays ≈2.2× rust `-O3`). The real wins are smaller/cleaner modules and the non-optimizing paths (browser metered interpreter, per-instruction gas). The residual fib gap is LLVM's recursion→accumulator-loop transform, beyond a peephole.

## Verification
- `cargo test -p kotoba-clj` → **216 passed / 0 failed** (193 prior + 23 new in `tests/coverage.rs`).
- A combined end-to-end program (`sort`+`take`+`reduce`+`merge`+`dotimes`) and the string/`str-int` paths run to identical results on **both** wasmtime and V8.
- `docs/ADR-clojure-wasm.md` records both batches incl. the honest peephole evaluation.

author: hiddentao
body:
## Why

Each search result's gray preview is just the first 200 chars of the item's text (`LEFT(field, 200)`). Because search ranks by **embedding similarity**, the typed term frequently doesn't appear in that lead text at all — so the preview never shows *why* a result matched (e.g. searching "mark" returns relevant items whose previews don't contain "mark").

This makes the preview a **context window centered on the query term, with the term highlighted**, so the match is self-explanatory.

### On the "should we switch to lunr.js?" question — no
- lunr is a **client-side** index, so adopting it would mean shipping every team's tasks/comments/docs the user can access to the browser to build the index — that breaks the team-scoped authorization model and leaks cross-team data.
- It also throws away semantic recall (synonyms, typos, conceptual matches) and wouldn't produce snippets for free anyway.

The feature is achievable on top of the existing embeddings with **no engine swap, no migration, and no new dependency**.

## What changed
- **`packages/server/src/lib/snippet.ts`** (new, pure util): builds a context window centered on the first literal match and wraps occurrences in a NUL sentinel. Strips markdown noise, handles multi-word queries, is case-insensitive with light stemming (`marking` ↔ `marked`), caps highlight count, and requires a word boundary for ≤2-char terms. Falls back to lead text on no match. `hasLiteralMatch` checks titles so a title-only match isn't mislabeled semantic-only.
- **`embeddings.ts`**: widen the 4 per-type snippet selects (`200` → `4000`) and shape each result through the util, setting the new `semanticOnly` flag.
- **shared**: add `HIGHLIGHT_SENTINEL` + optional `SearchResult.semanticOnly`.
- **web `search-results.tsx`**: render highlighted spans as `<mark>` by splitting on the sentinel (XSS-safe — React escapes each segment, no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`), switch the snippet line from `truncate` to `line-clamp-2`, and show a small **"related"** pill for semantic-only hits (so the absence of a highlight is explained).

## Behavior
- **Literal hit** → window centered on the term, every in-window occurrence highlighted, leading/trailing `…` as appropriate.
- **Semantic-only hit** (term in neither body nor title) → lead text, no highlight, **"related"** label.
- **Title-only hit** → lead-text body (no body highlight), no "related" label.

## Tests
- `packages/server/test/snippet.test.ts` (new): windowing, highlight, fallback, multi-word, start/middle/end ellipsis rules, case preservation, stemming, markdown stripping, short-term word boundary, null/empty, sentinel safety.
- `packages/server/test/embeddings.test.ts` (extended): proves the widened SQL + util compose over real PGlite rows and the `semanticOnly` logic.
- `packages/web/test/global-search.test.tsx` (extended): highlight rendering, the "related" label, and HTML escaping.

## Verification
- `bun run typecheck` ✓ · `bun run check` ✓ (0 errors)
- New/affected suites green: snippet (19), embeddings (17), web global-search (5)
- Full `bun run test --skip-browser`: server `2182 passed` / web `372 passed`. The only failures are 10 pre-existing, environment-related tests in `git.test.ts`/`ssh-agent-server.test.ts` (missing `ssh-keygen`/`ssh-add`) — verified identical on the clean baseline with these changes stashed.

PR ۱ از نقشه‌راهِ RBAC: بستنِ بالاترین ریسک‌های ارتقای امتیاز (privilege escalation) و جابه‌جاییِ بنیادینِ مدلِ نقش‌ها برای PR‌های بعدی.

## تغییرات (به چه دلیلی)

### بستنِ مسیرهای ارتقای امتیاز

- **`POST /register/`**: سریالایزر دیگر `orgRole`/`unitId` را نمی‌پذیرد و `RegisterView` به‌صورتِ defense-in-depth مقدار را hard-set می‌کند. دیگر نمی‌توان با ثبت‌نامِ عمومی خودرا `company_admin` کرد.
- **`PATCH /profile/`**: به همین دلیل دیگر نمی‌توان با پروفایل نقش/واحد خود را ارتقا داد.
- **`/manage-users/`**: به پرمیشن `CanManageUsers` و سریالایزرِ مجزای `AdminUserManagementSerializer` مرتبط شد. سطحِ شرکت دسترسیِ کامل دارد؛ مدیرانِ واحد (کسانی که واقعاً `OrgUnit.manager` هستند) فقط اعضای واحدهای تحتِ مدیریتِ خودشان را می‌بینند، و فقط می‌توانند نقش‌های `member`/`project_manager` را تخصیص دهند.
- **`/org-units/`**: خواندن برای هر کاربرِ احرازشده؛ ساخت/ویرایش/حذف فقط توسطِ سطحِ شرکت.

### اصلاحِ باگِ منطقی `manages_unit`

قبلاً هر کاربری با `org_role='unit_manager'` که عضوِ یک واحد بود خودبه‌خود مدیرِ آن واحد فرض می‌شد و اصلِ «یک مدیر برای هر واحد» را نقض می‌کرد. اکنون فقط `OrgUnit.manager` رسمی معتبر است.

### پایهٔ مدلِ نقش‌ها برای PR‌های بعدی

- نقشِ جدیدِ `project_manager` به `ORG_ROLES` افزوده شد تا چندین PM در یک واحد بتوانند پروژه بسازند بدونِ دادنِ دسترسیِ `unit_manager` به آن‌ها.
- `OrgUnit.is_planning_unit` با partial-unique constraint افزوده شد تا در PR‌های بعدی بتوانیم «مدیرِ برنامه‌ریزی» را در کد تشخیص دهیم.
- helperهای جدید در `ktcPlanning/permissions.py`: `get_planning_unit`, `get_planning_manager`, `is_planning_manager`, `effective_actor_ids` (آماده‌ساز delegation در آینده).
- BasePermission classes: `IsCompanyLevel`, `IsCompanyLevelOrReadOnly`, `CanManageUsers`.

### Hardening تنظیمات

- `SECRET_KEY`, `DEBUG`, `ALLOWED_HOSTS` از env با fallback برای dev.
- DRF throttling: نرخِ scoped برای `register` (5/min) + پیش‌فرض‌های `anon`/`user`.
- `SIMPLE_JWT`: `ROTATE_REFRESH_TOKENS=True` + `BLACKLIST_AFTER_ROTATION=True`.

## مهاجرت

`CustomUser/migrations/0003_planning_unit_and_project_manager_role.py`:
- AlterField روی `customuser.org_role` (تغییر choices).
- AddField روی `orgunit.is_planning_unit`.
- AddConstraint برای یکتایی شرطی.

## آنچه عمداً در این PR نیست (در PRهای بعدی)

- **PR ۲**: scoping خواندن (`accessible_projects`) برای پروژه/نسخه/تسک/گزارش.
- **PR ۳**: `Project.scope` + state machine برای `TaskReportLog` + singleton `SystemSettings` با تنظیمِ bypass + پیش‌فرضِ Approver = مدیرِ برنامه‌ریزی برای پروژهٔ شرکتی.
- **PR ۴**: `ProjectMembership` و یکپارچه‌سازیِ `ProjectViewer` + endpoint انتقالِ مالکیت.
- **PR ۵**: capabilities endpoint + delegation model.

## تست

- همه‌ی فایل‌های پایتونیِ تغییرکرده با `python -m py_compile` بدون خطا کامپایل شدند.
- اجرای `manage.py check`/`migrate` در این محیط (sandbox بدون شبکه) مقدور نبود؛ لطفاً به‌صورتِ محلی `python manage.py makemigrations --check --dry-run`، `python manage.py migrate`، و یک smoke test روی `/register/`، `/profile/`، `/manage-users/`، `/org-units/` انجام دهید.

## نکات سازگاری (compat)

- اگر فرانت‌اند هنگام ثبت‌نام `orgRole`/`unitId` ارسال می‌کرد، آن مقادیر اکنون silently ignored می‌شوند و کاربر با `member`/بدون واحد ساخته می‌شود (همان رفتارِ مطلوب). این یک تغییرِ behavioral نسبت به پیش است.
- مدیریتِ کاربران در UI همچنان از همان endpoint استفاده می‌کند، فقط دسترسی محدودتر شد. اگر کاربری که قبلاً صفحه‌ی Organization را می‌دید الان 403 می‌گیرد، انتظار درست است.

body:
Closes #67.

## Summary

- **New JSON rule type** `controller_has_ressource` on the existing power-unlock engine, honoured at the direct level and inside `OR` branches with strict amount validation (positive int required) and an opt-out `consume` flag that defaults to `true`. Composable with `controller_has_zone` for the canonical "free if you own the zone, pay if you traded it in" shape.
- **Commit-time re-validation** in `workers/action.php` closes the display→commit security gap on BOTH `transform` AND `teach_discipline` branches. A crafted GET that bypassed the form previously slipped past every JSON rule; now it re-runs `cleanPowerListFromJsonConditions` server-side and rejects with a French notification when the chosen power no longer survives the rule check. Admin / gm path keeps the legacy direct-upgrade behaviour as an intentional escape hatch.
- **Atomic ressource deduction** at commit time. New `consumeRessource(PDO, int controller_id, int ressource_id, int amount): bool` mirrors the `giftRessource` TOCTOU-safe pattern (`UPDATE … WHERE amount >= :amt`); the transform branch wraps `consumeRessource` + `upgradeWorker` in a transaction with rollback on either failure. Cross-resource cost stacking is suppressed with a logged warning (direct level takes precedence).
- **Shared `findMatchingBranch` helper** in `powers/functions.php` — single source of truth used by both the display filter (`cleanPowerListFromJsonConditions`) and the cost resolver (`getRuleCostForPower`). Eliminates display-vs-commit drift. Encodes the locked OR semantics: array-of-objects shape, keys-within-branch AND'd, branches OR'd, first-match-wins short-circuit.
- **`zone_name` gain-rule filter** on `ressourceGainMechanic` so per-zone gain rules can address zones by name rather than by CSV-row-order-coupled id.
- **Japon1555 economy expansion** — 4 new ressources (Cheval de Takamatsu, Armure en fer de Kubokawa, Thé d'Oboké, Encens Coréen) that accrue +1/turn on claim and +2/turn on hold of their producing zone. The 4 existing Shikoku transformations are retrofitted to an `OR: [{controller_has_zone}, {controller_has_ressource}]` gate so allies without the producing zone can still equip the transformation by paying 1 ressource received via the existing gift flow. 40 zero-amount `controller_ressources` seed rows added so the gain mechanic has rows to UPDATE.
- **`hide_when_zero` ressources_config flag** keeps these new scenario-specific currencies invisible on the player Ressources page until the controller has actually held them (strict threshold: hide only when `amount`, `amount_stored`, and `end_turn_gain` are all zero). Receive-side flows (gain, gift) ignore the flag, so a hidden ressource accrues silently and surfaces the moment it becomes non-zero.
- **Vampire1966 Possession fix** (inline R10): the `OR` was authored as a single-object form that PHP iterated as scalar keys, leaving the power fully hidden. Re-shaped to two single-key array branches so the original "age ≥ 2 OR worker inactive" intent finally renders.

## Test plan

- [x] `python3 -m pytest tests/test_transformation_unlock_rules_e2e.py -v` — 15 new tests (direct gate, opt-out consume, OR composition, D21 direct+OR cost, malformed amount, commit re-validation for transform + discipline, gm bypass, Vampire1966 Possession regression). All green in isolation.
- [x] `python3 -m pytest tests/test_hide_when_zero_ressource_e2e.py -v` — 3 new tests (hidden+zero hidden, non-zero visible, gift unaffected by filter). All green.
- [x] Pre-existing tests updated to reflect the new TestConfig CSV rows and the commit-time re-validation: `test_csv_features_e2e.py` power counts + `test_workers_action_auth_e2e.py` dead-worker carve-out URL now carries a valid `transformation` id.
- [x] Full local suite: `443 passed in 21:51` (425 baseline + 15 + 3 new).
- [x] Manual sanity (player path): non-privileged player triggers a transform whose Gold cost they can no longer pay → notification, no `worker_powers` insert.
- [x] Manual sanity (admin path): gm path still grants any transformation regardless of rules and never deducts.
- [x] Japon1555CSV full reset clean — checked via `test_full_reset_japon1555_csv`.

## Out of scope / deferred

- Harmonising `spendRessourcesToMoveBase` + `spendRessourcesToRepairLocation` with the new `consumeRessource` primitive (silent-success on insufficient stock is a known pre-existing surface).
- Extending the OR-block to also honour `controller_faction` + `worker_in_zone` (only zone and ressource honoured in this PR).
- A general non-power `cost_resource` mechanic.
- Multi-resource stacking inside one rule (current policy: direct precedence + warning).

## Authoring conventions locked

Documented in `docs/configuration.md`:

- `OR` is an array of objects; one rule per branch is the recommended shape (keys within a branch are AND'd).
- Cheaper / non-consuming branches go first in the array (first-match-wins).
- `consume` defaults to `true` — write `consume: false` to opt out of deduction explicitly.

author: masein
body:
Log employee/contractor hours against a client (+ optional project), then generate a professional client invoice from unbilled time at the worker's **billable rate**, post it to AR, and download a **branded, project-grouped PDF**. Reuses the existing invoice/AR engine — no parallel accounting path.

## Data model (migration `014`, additive/nullable)
- `billable_rate` on `EmployeePayProfile` — **separate from payroll cost**.
- **`Project`** (belongs to a client), **`BillingRateOverride`** (rate scoped to project/client/default), **`TimeEntry`** (worker = employee **or** supplier/contractor; client required; optional project; `billable`; status `unbilled|invoiced|written_off`; `invoice_id` back-reference + `rate_snapshot`).

## Billing service
- **Rate precedence**: project → client → default override → `profile.billable_rate`.
- Aggregate unbilled (billable only) **grouped by project → employee**; build a preview (subtotal/VAT/total, period, exact entries); `create_invoice_from_time` reuses `create_invoice` → posts **DR trade debtors / CR sales / CR output VAT** (balanced incl VAT, single per-line rounding), stamps entries `invoiced` + `rate_snapshot`. **Voiding** the invoice **un-bills** its entries (atomic). **Mixed-currency** unbilled time is blocked, not merged. Invoiced time is **locked**.

## REST API (`/time`) + PDF
projects · billable rates · time entries (grid CRUD, write-off, lock invoiced) · `/unbilled` (Ready-to-invoice) · `invoice-preview` · `invoice` · branded **time-invoice PDF** (grouped by project, `employee · hours · rate · amount`, subtotal/VAT/total, bank details, **timesheet appendix**). `void` un-bill hook added to the invoice path; `reset-db` wipes the new tables.

## AI tools (confirm-gated, audited)
- **read**: `list_unbilled_time`, `get_time_summary`.
- **proposal**: `propose_log_time` (**one card** even when it creates a new worker/client/project — freelancer→supplier), `propose_create_project`, `propose_set_billable_rate`, `propose_create_invoice_from_time` (shows the **exact entries/hours/value** before Confirm). Execute handlers + orchestrator guidance.

## Frontend (Time tab) + i18n
Log time, new project, set rate, entries table (status colours + lock 🔒), **Ready-to-invoice** panel, **invoice preview grouped by project**, one-click create + **PDF download**. New strings in all four packs (en/fa/es/ar).

Issuing a time invoice is **not** routed through the outgoing-payment approval threshold (that's for money leaving); only the later client *payment* touches cash.

## Acceptance (tests, UK + Iran)
- Rate precedence project>client>default>profile ✅
- Aggregation/grouping by project→employee; subtotal correct ✅
- Invoice journal **balanced incl VAT** (`DR 1100 / CR 4000 / CR 2200`; Iran equivalents); entries flip to `invoiced` and are **excluded from re-invoicing** (no double-bill) ✅
- **Void → entries return to unbilled** ✅
- **Multi-currency guard** blocks; non-billable never invoices; **invoiced entry locked** (409); empty selection → friendly no-op ✅
- AI: log time creating **new client+project+worker in one card** (freelancer→supplier); set-rate; invoice-from-time propose→execute ✅
- PDF renders (smoke-checked). `pytest -q` green incl. **translation parity** (703 passed; the one local `test_anthropic_config` failure is a `.env` base-URL leak, passes in CI).

> Backend changes need `docker compose up -d --build api` (migration `014` adds `projects`, `billing_rate_overrides`, `time_entries`, `employee_pay_profiles.billable_rate`).

**Where rates are set / how to download:** set a billable rate in the **Time** tab ("Set billable rate…", scoped to the selected client/project or the worker default) or via chat ("set Sarah's rate to 90 for OTL"). Create an invoice from the **Ready to invoice** panel (preview → Create) or chat ("invoice Acme for the OTL hours") — the **PDF opens/downloads** on create, and is always available at `/time/invoice/{id}/pdf`.

## Doesn't regress
PR #35/#36 one-card collapse + freelancer→supplier; supplier-payment direction; customer-receipt→trade-debtors; worded dates; approval routing; OCR decimal fix; existing manual Invoices/AR flow.
